title: Regional minimum wage returns to debate in Rio Grande do Sul elections
seoTitle: RS Elections: Regional Minimum Wage Returns to Debate
subtitle: Gubernatorial candidates in Rio Grande do Sul present differing stances on maintaining and adjusting the regional wage floor
excerpt: Ahead of elections, the regional minimum wage emerges as a central theme in the economic proposals of Rio Grande do Sul gubernatorial candidates, generating.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
With the state election approaching, the regional minimum wage is taking center stage in the platforms of candidates for governor of Rio Grande do Sul. The issue divides business owners and workers, emerging as a point of contention in the economic proposals presented in recent weeks.

Juliana Brizola's stance on the regional wage floor

Juliana Brizola (PDT) stated that she will favor the regional minimum wage. In an interview, the candidate declared support for the floor without mentioning tax increases, and emphasized her intention to discuss adjustments with the business sector.

Marcelo Maranata proposes eliminating the wage floor

Marcelo Maranata (PSDB) advocates for eliminating the regional minimum wage. The candidate plans to remove the wage floor while simultaneously seeking state participation as a partner in companies and strengthening Banrisul.

Luciano Zucco maintains defense of the regional minimum wage

Luciano Zucco (PL) favors maintaining the regional minimum wage and indicates that adjustments will be negotiated with the business sector. Additionally, Zucco mentions reassessing the renewal of South Summit.

Gabriel Souza also supports the regional wage floor

Gabriel Souza (MDB) assures that he will maintain the regional minimum wage, discussing its adjustment with business leaders. The candidate also highlights the continuation of waterway dredging and negotiations to extend the suspension of the state's debt with the Federal Government.

Expected impacts on workers and businesses

The differing proposals indicate that maintaining or eliminating the regional wage floor could influence workers' purchasing power and the competitiveness of companies in Rio Grande do Sul. While candidates defending the regional minimum wage point to the need for negotiated adjustments, the candidate proposing its elimination seeks to simplify the cost structure.

With reporting from GZH, Matinal, Expansão.
